title: Failure Response
shortDefinition: Failure response is the plan for the moment the first technique is blocked.
whyItMatters: The failure moment is where many people freeze, overcommit, or expose neck, back, or legs.
deepExplanation: A good system defines: if inside position is lost, reset; if they turn away, take back; if they frame, change angle. Failure is not stopping; it is branching.
beginnerView: Know what to do when the move does not work.
advancedView: Design techniques so the first failure opens the second option.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Failure Response during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Failure Response to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Failure Response is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Failure Response before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
